title.value: Guiding The Last Layer in Federated Learning with Pre-Trained Models
title.justification: The title is derived directly from the paper, indicating the main focus on guiding the last layer in federated learning using pre-trained models.
title.quote: Guiding The Last Layer in Federated Learning with Pre-Trained Models Gwen Legate Concordia University, Mila Montreal, Canada

extractions.description: The paper discusses a method in Federated Learning (FL) using pre-trained models, focusing on improving the efficiency and performance of FL algorithms. It introduces a two-stage approach for transfer learning in the FL setting, initially using the Nearest Class Means (NCM) method to optimize the classification head followed by fine-tuning the entire model. This new approach aims to reduce communication and computation costs while enhancing model performance. The FedNCM allows efficient initialization and significant gains in FL settings, especially under non-iid data distributions.

primary_category.justification: Although the paper mainly addresses Federated Learning's efficiency and effectiveness, these improvements could potentially lead to more efficient AI models, thereby reducing the computational resources required for various applications. This aligns broadly with the goals of 'Climate Change Mitigation' focusing on reducing resource use and emissions indirectly.
primary_category.quote: We demonstrate the potential our method has to reduce communication and compute costs while achieving better model performance.
